about: Which team each session belongs to, for machines. teams/README.md is the text people read, and the two are kept in step. The session-observability plugin puts the team in every binding line (jgwill/miadi-orchestration-kit#56). Rules, in order: a declared team (MIADI_TEAM in the agent's environment, or the tmux session option @miadi-team), then sessions (the tmux session name or the agent session's name), then folders (the agent's folder or one below it, longest prefix wins), then name_patterns (regular expressions on the same two names). Otherwise the team is unassigned.
criteria_about: criteria: each team's responsibility as a program reads it, so that a piece of work can be matched to the team that carries it (the routing step proposed in Episode 575's staging folder routing-a-decomposition-to-teams-261113, tried as an alpha in jgwill/mia-code `miaco route`). desired_outcome and makes are taken from each team's section of teams/README.md, quoting William where the README does. Only T8's section writes a boundary; the others were read from their sections' words on 2026-11-13 by the seat t8-miaco-route-alpha-2611132120, for each team's lead to correct. Change the README and these fields together.

criteria.desired_outcome: After a reboot or a crash every terminal session comes back as it was, with the agent it held. William, 2026-09-28: "I should not even know that the computer rebooted."
criteria.makes: The capture hooks and the binding line (every agent session's start, end and rename with its tmux pane, launch, team and episode), tmux save and restore, tide's agent restore and snapshots, the session-observability plugins for Claude, Pi and Hermes, the session inventory format and the nightly inventory, and boot safety on gaia.
criteria.boundary: The machine and the terminal layer: what keeps sessions alive and recorded. It does not build the Miadi app or shared packages (T8) and does not judge what a session produced (T3).

criteria.desired_outcome: Miadi knows which events travel, what stays attached to them, and how anyone can see that an event arrived or visibly failed.
criteria.makes: The event broker choice and its first proof (Episode 548), the trace, prompt and metric addresses and the door that opens them from a terminal or a page, and @miadi/llmops.
criteria.boundary: Events and traces between the parts of the factory. Keeping sessions alive is T1's, and charts are T4's.

criteria.boundary: A chart here is a structural tension chart (desired outcome, current reality, action steps) kept in a coaia-narrative .jsonl memory. Trading charts and stateloom drawings are not its work.
